- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) are common; cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high or 1.2x prior peak.
- Model often overreacts to sentiment shifts; lag correction: if sentiment changes direction, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate later months (especially 20–30 days) when sentiment is bullish; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per 5-day horizon.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days for smoothing.
- Avoid forecasting spikes if sentiment is weak or negative; if sentiment turns bullish, allow 1–2 day lag before adjusting forecast upward.
